rows.annotation: The quantifier `∀ᵐ ω` encloses continuity, the initial value and the universal equation over `Set.Icc 0 1`. Thus a single null set is removed for all $0\le t\le1$, including both endpoints.

rows.annotation: The field `progressive` uses `incrementFiltration W t`, generated by $B_{t+s}-B_t$ as elapsed time $s$ varies. The field `bound` requires $|\alpha_s(\omega)|\le1$ for every $s\ge0$ and every $\omega$, without an exceptional null set.

rows.annotation: The coefficient of `perturbation γ β n` is $\gamma+(\beta-\gamma)/(n+1)$, because `variationStep n` equals $1/(n+1)$. The conclusion concerns only these sampled difference quotients, so identifying an ordinary feasible right derivative requires a further argument.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Heat.finite_density_coercivity

rows.annotation: The equality `he` rewrites `finiteDensity` as `gaussianLogDensity d U`, after which the final line applies `gaussian_shape_coercivity`. The shape and regularity hypotheses for that application are established for the finite-step data earlier in the proof.

rows.note: This supplier obtains the whole-line inequality using positive-half-line flux and reflection.
rows.annotation: The proof integrates the certificate derivative over $(0,\infty)$, where the shape hypothesis gives $r(x)>0$, and uses zero boundary flux at the origin and infinity. Evenness of the density and both integrands then doubles the half-line inequality to obtain the whole-line bound.

rows.annotation: The conjunction in `value_consequences` ends with equality for a supplied minimiser. Before it are `ScalarValueConclusion` for a supplied diffusion and `FiniteGaussianConclusion` for that diffusion and an interior cutoff.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.sourceStripRegularity
rows.note: This theorem provides the strip bounds for every admissible scalar coefficient, before minimization is used.
rows.annotation: For each $0\leq T<1$, `SourceStripRegularity` gives a uniform curvature bound and joint time-space Lipschitz bounds for the gradient and curvature on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R$. The theorem takes only `W` and the admissible `γ`.

rows.plain: If the squared-gradient moment equals t, the squared-curvature moment equals one
rows.annotation: The proof uses contact to identify the primitive of the curvature square moment with $t$, then differentiates it on $(0,1)$. Continuity from `hreg` extends the resulting value $1$ to $t=0$.

ties.name: OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.finite_gaussian_fixed_strip
ties.plain: Shifted Gaussian convergence under strip bounds and unit curvature moment

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.finite_gaussian_fixed_strip
rows.note: This internal helper takes the strip constants and curvature second moment as explicit premises.
rows.plain: Shifted Gaussian convergence under strip bounds and unit curvature moment
rows.annotation: The strip bounds and unit curvature moment on the closed interval $[0,T]$ are explicit premises here. The two conjuncts give eventual positivity and the $N\to\infty$ sum limit at fixed $T<1$, leaving the terminal cutoff limit to another argument.

rows.name: OAI.SKValueG.groundStateSequence_tendsto
rows.annotation: `groundStateValue` names a limit candidate by `limUnder`. The `Tendsto` theorem supplies convergence of the finite-spin mean energies to that value independently of the variational minimiser.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.euler
rows.note: The $N$ updates consume formal coordinates 0 through $N-1$; coordinate $N$ is reserved for rounding.
rows.annotation: For $N>0$, the recursion starts at zero and evaluates the drift at $(t_j,Y_j)$ with $t_j=jT/N$. Update $j\mapsto j+1$ uses `coordinate N j`, so the first $N$ updates consume the first $N$ Gaussians and leave coordinate $N$ unused.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.normalizer
rows.note: Formal $j=0,\dots,N-1$ corresponds to $c_{1},\dots,c_N$.
rows.annotation: For $j<N$, the definition gives $\bigl(\sqrt{\mathbb E[a(t_j,Y_j)^2]}\bigr)^{-1}$, so $j=0,\ldots,N-1$ corresponds to $c_1,\ldots,c_N$. Positivity is a separate assertion, since the reciprocal square root is zero when the second moment is zero.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.FiniteGaussianConclusion
rows.note: Every active index is positive for each mesh beyond one common threshold.
rows.plain: The shifted Gaussian sums converge to the mean-curvature integral at fixed cutoff
rows.annotation: Only `j < N` appears in the positivity clause, so it covers $c_1,\ldots,c_N$ through source indices $0,\ldots,N-1$. No positivity claim is made for `normalizer W γ T N N`, despite its total definition.

rows.fidelity_note: The definition identifies the last coordinate used for rounding. Preservation of the conditional mean also requires the separate Gaussian-rounding integral lemma.
rows.name: OAI.SKValue.roundedSign
rows.note: Identifies the fresh rounding coordinate; mean preservation is proved separately.
rows.annotation: `cdf standardGaussian` is applied to `coordinate N N z`, so the added term uses the paper’s $Z_{N+1}$. The first $N$ Euler steps use only the earlier coordinates.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.coefficientB
rows.note: At $i=N+1$, `coefficientB` uses coordinate $N$.
rows.annotation: At $i=N+1$, the index `i-1` is $N$, so the integral defining $B_{N+1}$ pairs the rounded sign with $Z_{N+1}$.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.shiftedCoefficientSum
rows.note: `Finset.range (N+1)` is exactly $j=0,\dots,N$.
rows.annotation: The range `Finset.range (N+1)` contains exactly $j=0,\ldots,N$, and the second factor is evaluated at $j+1$. The definition of `coefficientA` makes the $j=0$ summand vanish, while the last summand uses $B_{N+1}$.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.coordinate
rows.note: Within the active range, coordinate `N j` is the $(j+1)$st paper Gaussian.
rows.annotation: For $0\le j\le N$, the remainder `j % (N+1)` equals $j$, so `coordinate N j` reads the paper's $Z_{j+1}$. The modulus makes the definition total for larger natural indices and introduces no wraparound among the active coordinates.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.rawCoefficient
rows.note: This coefficient is $a(t_j,Y_j)$, before multiplication by a fresh Gaussian.
rows.plain: Curvature at a left mesh point
rows.annotation: The arguments of `curvature` are `meshTime T N j` and the Euler value after $j$ updates, giving $a(t_j,Y_j)$. No factor of `coordinate N j` appears until the separate definition of `gaussianIncrement`.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.normalizer
rows.note: The inverse square root of that coefficient’s second moment is $c_{j+1}$.
rows.annotation: At Lean index $j<N$, first integrate the square of `rawCoefficient` over the Gaussian product measure. The reciprocal square root of the result is the deterministic weight $c_{j+1}$ multiplying the random coefficient.

ties.name: OAI.SKValue.FiniteGaussianConclusion
ties.plain: The shifted Gaussian sums converge to the mean-curvature integral at fixed cutoff

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.FiniteGaussianConclusion
rows.note: `∀ᶠ N in atTop` means one $N_{0}$ works for every later $N$ and every $j<N$.
rows.plain: The shifted Gaussian sums converge to the mean-curvature integral at fixed cutoff
rows.annotation: The nesting gives one $N_0$ such that every $N\ge N_0$ and every $j<N$ satisfy positivity. Since $T$ is fixed before this assertion, the threshold may depend on $T$ and no uniform threshold over cutoffs is asserted.

rows.plain: Gradient stopped at the terminal spin
rows.annotation: The time $t=1$ already takes the `else` branch, so the process equals $U$ on all $t\ge1$ and uses the diffusion gradient only for $0\le t<1$.

ties.plain: The terminal spin has Brownian correlation equal to the scalar ground-state value

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.ScalarValueConclusion
rows.note: The almost-sure and mean-square limits both approach one from below.
rows.plain: The terminal spin has Brownian correlation equal to the scalar ground-state value
rows.annotation: The same existential $U$ appears in the almost-sure condition $(U\omega)^2=1$ and both convergence clauses. In each clause `𝓝[<] 1` means approach from below, while the second `Tendsto` expresses $L^2$ convergence by $\mathbb E[(u(t,X_t)-U)^2]\to0$.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.terminal_gradient_product
rows.note: The hypotheses are diffusion, eventual differentiability and a terminal gradient limit; there is no no-atom premise.
rows.plain: The terminal slope satisfies UX₁ = |X₁| almost surely
rows.annotation: The proof handles $X_1=0$ separately, where both sides vanish. For $X_1\ne0$, eventual differentiability `hd` and the terminal limits identify $U=\operatorname{sign}(X_1)$, yielding the product identity without a no-atom assumption.

rows.note: This is a real-time function with shape conditions on $[0,1)$; the restriction map itself is an obligation.
rows.annotation: The `coeff` field has domain $\mathbb R$, while `nonneg` and `monotone` concern only $[0,1)$. Restricting `coeff` to `Time` must also preserve the required right continuity and supply integrability of the zero extension.

ties.plain: A probability space with Brownian motion

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.BrownianSystem
rows.note: The support model leaves $Ω$ and its measurable space as external parameters.
rows.plain: A probability space with Brownian motion
rows.annotation: Here $\Omega$ and its measurable space are external parameters, while `law` and `B` are fields of the structure. A transport must retain these data on the same space before comparing the natural and increment filtrations.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.BrownianSpace
rows.note: The scalar model bundles $Ω$ and its measurable space along with the law and Brownian motion.
rows.annotation: `BrownianSpace` packages the sample type `Ω`, `measurableSpace`, the law `μ` and process `B`. Its measurability field is also data needed when relating the two formal Brownian systems.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.Admissible
rows.note: A predicate requiring progressive measurability for elapsed Brownian increments and a pointwise bound.
rows.annotation: The scalar control remains an ordinary function $\alpha$, with admissibility expressed by the two conjuncts. They require progressivity for `shiftedFiltration W t` and $|\alpha_s(\omega)|\le1$ for every $s,\omega$, so an almost-everywhere bound would not suffice.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Control
rows.note: The same kinds of conditions are fields in a bundled control; no conversion theorem is asserted here.
rows.annotation: A `Control` bundles the process in `val` together with proofs of progressivity and the pointwise bound. Moving a scalar admissible process into this structure requires identifying `shiftedFiltration` with `incrementFiltration` on the chosen Brownian space, a conversion not supplied by this declaration.

ties.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.controlPayoff
ties.plain: Reward minus the quadratic control cost

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.controlPayoff
rows.note: A pathwise payoff uses absolute time $s$ from $t$ to one and the elapsed control argument $s-t$.
rows.plain: Reward minus the quadratic control cost
rows.annotation: Both integrals use absolute time $s\in[t,1]$ and evaluate the control at `Real.toNNReal (s - t)`, once linearly and once squared. This payoff is pathwise, with expectation taken later in `value`.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.controlPayoff
rows.note: The scalar payoff includes expectation and writes its time integral in elapsed time r.
rows.annotation: Here the integration variable is elapsed time, so `γ.coeff (t+s)` evaluates the coefficient at absolute time and `α (Real.toNNReal s)` uses the elapsed control value. The outer integral already takes expectation, unlike the support model's pathwise payoff.

rows.fidelity_note: This is the support-model definition of minimality over all support OrderParameter competitors, not a proof transporting those competitors to the scalar model.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.IsMinimizer
rows.annotation: The support-model quantifier ranges over `ZeroTemperatureSK.OrderParameter` on the given `BrownianSystem`. To use the same comparison for the scalar model, a competitor and its value must be related to the corresponding scalar objects.

rows.fidelity_note: This is the scalar-model definition of minimality over all scalar OrderParameter competitors, not a theorem relating the two minimizer predicates.
rows.name: OAI.SKValue.IsMinimizer
rows.annotation: Here `η` ranges over scalar-model order parameters and the Brownian space is the scalar `BrownianSpace`. The displayed definition makes a comparison within that model.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.IsDiffusion
rows.note: Progressivity is required of X on all nonnegative times; its equation is restricted to [0,1].
rows.annotation: The first conjunct requires `IsProgressive` for the whole nonnegative-time process `X`. The second conjunct restricts continuity and the path equation to $[0,1]$ outside a single null set.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion
rows.note: The stopped process must be adapted; almost-sure continuity is specified on [0,1].
rows.annotation: The adapted process is $t\mapsto X_{\min(t,1)}$ for nonnegative $t$, so values of $X$ after one do not enter this condition. Continuity and the path equation hold on $[0,1]$ outside one null set, with no global progressivity premise.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Certificate.remainder
rows.note: The explicit 22-term polynomial; positivity of its values also needs sign conditions on its variables.
rows.annotation: The $v^4$ coefficient is $1661507/1521000000=1/1000+140507/1521000000$. All 22 coefficients are positive rationals, so at nonnegative $R,K,v,B,j$ the remaining 21 terms can be discarded in a lower bound.

rows.fidelity_note: Lean states only $\frac{1}{1000}<\frac{1661507}{1521000000}$. The paper additionally states the exact difference $\frac{140507}{1521000000}$; that equality is not the theorem's conclusion.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Certificate.coercivity_constant
rows.note: Strict positivity of the surplus; the displayed exact difference is further rational arithmetic.
rows.annotation: `coercivity_constant` proves the strict comparison of $1661507/1521000000$ with $1/1000$. Subtracting with a common denominator gives the exact surplus in the selected sentence.
